headline: Discussed use of cannabis tax stabilization fund, with approximately $1.7 million remaining and no funding allocations or recommendations made.
summary: Discussed how cannabis tax revenue is deposited and how the Cannabis Stabilization Fund may be used. The fund has approximately $1.7 million remaining after a prior repayment of approximately $1.4 million to two cannabis businesses. No funding allocations or formal recommendations were made.

Public Portion 
 1. Discussion on Cannabis Tax Revenue 
On October 13, 2026, the Finance Committee, chaired by Councilor Zaida Govan, met to discuss 
cannabis tax revenue and the City's Cannabis Stabilization Fund. The committee reviewed how 
33% of cannabis tax revenue is deposited into the stabilization fund, with the remainder allocated 
to the General Fund. The City previously repaid approximately $1.4 million to two cannabis 
businesses after state law determined that additional fees collected under host community 
agreements were unallowable. The repayment was made from the stabilization fund, which 
currently has approximately $1.7 million remaining. 
 
The committee reviewed fund deposits of approximately $543,000 in FY2025 and $609,000 in 
FY2026, along with $1.2 million in cannabis tax revenue allocated to the General Fund in 
FY2026. The stabilization fund is designated for educational and recreational programs, 
neighborhood business incentives, infrastructure improvements, recreational and community 
sites, and other eligible initiatives within 1.5 miles of cannabis establishments. 
 
Discussion focused on using available funds to address neighborhood impacts, identifying 
eligible projects, and exploring the possibility of supporting targeted property tax relief. City 
financial representatives explained that accessing the funds would require coordination with the 
Mayor and City Council approval through a financial order. Expanding the fund's permitted uses 
would require changes to the existing authorization. The committee discussed establishing 
funding priorities, identifying neighborhood needs, and working with City officials to determine 
the process for allocating available funds. Additional discussion included improving public 
awareness of the City's targeted property tax relief program. No funding allocations or formal 
recommendations were made. The meeting adjourned at 4:22 p.m.
